thread:
marta: heads-up — on the int4 experiment for the new hybrid-head model I saw repeated subtoken glue in several long-context prompts, and some weird rotary phase artifacts near token boundaries.
liam: can you paste an example output? is this on the ll->mistral conversion branch? :thinking:
marta: yep, conversion branch `onboard/hybrid-heads/v2`, quantized with our int4 pipeline. minimal repro: `python serve_local.py --model ./converted --quant int4 --prompt 'In the year 2060, the committee decided...' --max_tokens 256`
choi: logs? maybe kv cache warmup mismatch or token id aliasing. those often show as repeated subtokens.
marta: paste of generation snippet: 
```
Input: "… decided to create a pan-continental archive of language."
Output: "… decided to create a pan-continental arch@@ ive of lang@@ uage. the archive arch@@ ive kept…"
```
liam: that `@@` is the byte-level subtoken marker from the tokenizer, right? so we're seeing glue/merge twice. could be tokenizer normalization vs exported vocab mapping.
marta: tokenizer mapping looked fine on the surface. but when I diff token ids post-conversion, some subtokens map to adjacent ids (off-by-one clusters) for the last 128 IDs. suspect aliasing from our custom merge table.
ops-bot: new build deployed for `onboard/hybrid-heads/v2` at 2026-03-12T14:02Z :rocket:
choi: second issue is the rotary phase artifact — near those glued subtokens logits show periodic oscillation across heads. quick FFT of attention phase shows spikes at head groups 4 and 5.
liam: that smells like a head-shard ordering mismatch. when we shard heads for per-head rotary params, any reordering during conversion or serialization will cause the sin/cos to apply to wrong head slices. leads to phase-warp on boundaries where subtokens cross attention window.
marta: here's the KV cache dump excerpt (head 4, timestep 42):
```
# kv_cache[head=4][t=42][:8]
[0.012, -0.345, 0.002, ... , -0.110]
# after quant decode -> dequantized
[0.014, -0.342, 0.001, ... , -0.112]
```
choi: quantitatively similar but phase sign flips on a subset of heads? could be our int4 dequant table using per-tile scales but we used global for export, or vice-versa.
liam: action plan: 1) repro with full-precision (fp16) converted weights to confirm quant is the culprit; 2) run tokenizer id audit to check contiguous ranges and any remapped ids; 3) assert head ordering invariants during model.save() and conversion (write a small test that compares `orig.head_index` -> `loaded.head_index`).
marta: doing (1) now — starting fp16 run. if fp16 is clean, that points at quant tables or int4 packing.
ops-bot: eval-batch queued (job id eval-1034) — will run through perf+quality suite and post results here. ETA ~ 8m.
liam: for tokenizer audit, run `python scripts/token_audit.py --orig tok.json --converted tok_converted.json --report token_audit.html` — it highlights reorders and duplicate ids. also check for invisible joiner tokens (ZWJ, soft-hyphen) getting normalized differently. those cause weird glue.
choi: also add a small test to verify rotary params: compute sincos matrices for first 16 positions and assert elementwise equality between reference and converted model (tolerance 1e-6 for fp16, 1e-2 for int4-dequant). if mismatch -> report head reorder.
marta: fp16 run initial — looks a lot better: no doubled subtokens, and attention phases stable. eval-bot: eval-1034 finished: speed 1.9x baseline, perplexity delta +0.05 (fp16).
liam: ok that isolates quant path. could be our int4 packer applying blockwise scales with wrong stride when model has hybrid head layouts. i've seen this when block size assumes contiguous head dims but conversion interleaves heads for fused kernels.
choi: i can attempt to re-run quant pipeline with `--preserve-head-layout` flag and output a diagnostic mapping. try that next.
marta: will run preserve-head-layout + token audit and post artifacts. thanks. :thumbsup:
liam: if that fixes it we should add a CI gate: run token-audit + head-layout-check for any conversion to int4 and fail early. less manual triage later.
ops-bot: reminder: conversion artifacts should be uploaded to s3://redwood-onboard/artifacts/hybrid-heads/v2/7390012345 within 24h.
choi: noted. if preserve-head-layout still fails, next step is to compare quantizer scale tables per-tile between reference and converted; mismatch means we used different zero points/scales during packing.
marta: uploaded token_audit.html + kv_dumps to s3. linking: https://s3.redwood.internal/artifacts/7390012345/token_audit.html :eyes:
liam: opened report — shows small cluster of remapped ids at end of vocab (indices 50240-50287) that overlap with special joiner set. that correlates with the gluing. good catch.
choi: i'll start a repro with `--preserve-head-layout` now and also add the rotary matrix equality check to quantizer unit tests.
marta: great. i'll wait for the int4 repro before filing a formal bug. thanks team.
